content:
Now that 2026 is half over, what are you prioritizing as work goals? 
Goals are defined, with deadlines and details that can help you stay on track. 
In sales, there are:
➡️ Prospecting goals - how many people will you actually TALK TO or have meaningful conversations with in text, email, or in a DM? 
➡️ Customer care goals - how many existing clients or customers will you or someone on your team reach out to? NOT just when you're told their coming up for renewal. 
➡️ Personal health goals - for me, it is getting outside every day (I'm in Arizona where it is HOT now, so I have to plan mindfully) Also I get up every hour and walk. 
➡️ Referral goals - yes, is part of prospecting but important to segment out. Did you make a list of 10 or 20 or 30 people who can refer you to many? They are in adjacent businesses or sectors, like marketing expertise to my sales expertise? I refer great marketers because their solutions don't usually work if there are poor sellers at their clients' company. And my sales strategies don't work when marketing is missing or poor. That is one of the most perfect referrer relationships - we should talk every few weeks. How big is your list? 
I learned the hard way the value of setting goals - especially tied to growing revenues. If you need help, reach out. 

“Whenever you want to achieve something, keep your eyes open, concentrate and make sure you know exactly what it is you want. No one can hit their target with their eyes closed.”
― Paulo Coelho, The Devil and Miss Prym                                     #createimpact #seeitbeit
personaInterest: Setting and achieving sales goals, particularly prospecting and referral goals
keyTakeaway: Target sales professionals struggling with scalability and offer goal-setting strategies to help them achieve revenue growth through effective prospecting and referral tactics.

content:
It's the last 3 days of the quarter. Americans are getting ready for 4th of July at the end of next week. Now is the time to double down on your connects and outreach. 
TIPS: 
➡️ make extra time on outreach today. 
➡️ use a multifaceted approach (LinkedIn, phone, email)
➡️ if you believe in your product or service it is upon you to keep reaching out until you hear something from your future customer. 
➡️ if nothing else, get meetings set up for next month on the calendar now. 
➡️ focus on your buyer's needs and interests, not yours
➡️ know who your ideal customer is and what is important to them before you reach out to them. 
➡️ smile while you dial (thanks for the reminder, @sam nelson) 
➡️ have an abundant mindset. See yourself as successful 
➡️ focus, focus, focus. Get an accountability partner if you can. You can do it.
keyTakeaway: Sales teams should intensify multifaceted outreach efforts, focusing on buyer needs and ideal customer profiles, to maximize end-of-quarter results.

It's today, Arizona! If you are in the Phoenix area, come join us! The Pavilion Phoenix Chapter is hosting an amazing session led by my colleague and chapter co-lead Jen Spencer on how marketing is changing and some incredible insights as to what those in GTM can be thinking about. Thank you to Booth for being our local sponsor. 

In a world where AI agents, global talent, and flexible labor are reshaping how work gets done, marketing leaders are rethinking what their teams actually need to look like. This session creates space to explore that question together — through a short framework, real examples, and a hands-on exercise attendees can walk away using immediately.  Comment in the post and I'll send the details, and Pavilion events are always listed on the website.

content:
Downsized in real time? This really happened. Over the weekend a colleague reached out to me and wanted to connect me to someone in a venture firm as they thought it would be a great intro for both of us. He made an intro by email. I reached out with email reply on Monday to thank the person for thinking of me, and asking the connection for her calendar link. 

She replied happily with the link and suggested we jump on a call. About an hour or two later, when I read her email reply (same afternoon), I went ahead and clicked the link. Surprisingly it didn't work - maybe she copied it wrong to me? Anyway, I tried again - nope. 

So I sent her a reply to her email to say, "hey, that link didn't work - maybe you sent me the wrong one?" An hour goes by, and someone ELSE from that company replies that she is NO LONGER WITH THE COMPANY. What?? 

I feel bad for her. She was in an executive role and clearly had NO idea of what was happening. I told my friend and colleague about this and I'm hoping he reached out to her to make sure she is OK. Corporate did not used to be this cutthroat. It was like the dice rolled, and she got, "Do not pass GO." #Rantover
personaInterest: Supporting colleagues who have been unexpectedly let go
keyTakeaway: Target companies undergoing restructuring may have urgent needs for outplacement services or executive support solutions.
